stepBody:
Consider the matrix $$X$$ whose five rows are
• $$(0, 2, -1)$$
• $$(0, 2, -2)$$
• $$(1, 1, -3)$$
• $$(1, 1, -4)$$
• $$(2, 0, -5)$$
Let $$P$$ be the principal component matrix of $$X.$$ That is,
$$P= \cup {\Sigma}$$
Suppose we now decompose the principal component matrix $$P$$ into its principal components, giving us
$$P=U_{P}\Sigma_PV_P**{T}$$
What is $$V_P**{T}$$
answerLatex: The $$3$$ by $$3$$ identity matrix, with rows (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (0,0,1)
choices: The $$3$$ by $$3$$ identity matrix, with rows (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (0,0,1)
The $$3$$ by $$3$$ matrix of all zeros, with rows (0,0,0), (0,0,0) and (0,0,0)
The $$2$$ by $$2$$ identity matrix, with rows $$(1,0)$$ and $$(0,1)$$
The same matrix as $$V**{T}$$ obtained from the decomposition of $$X$$
